actors.name: Alex
actors.scope: Confirmed stock, the latest supplier ETA and dispatch cutoffs.

questions.label: What stock is available right now?
questions.response: We have {onHand} study kits on hand. The additional {replenishment} are expected stock; I have not recorded them as received.

questions.label: When is the replenishment expected?
questions.response: Our latest supplier notice says {eta} for the {replenishment} kits. That is an expected arrival, not a receipt. Each departure can use them only if they arrive by its staging cutoff.

questions.label: What are the dispatch cutoffs?
questions.response: Here is the dispatch schedule. Each departure has one shared capacity across all orders. Kits need to be available by its cutoff; the arrival time determines which delivery promise it can meet.

actors.name: Jordan
actors.scope: Our own order and delivery arrangements we can accept.

questions.label: What delivery promise is currently recorded?
questions.response: For our {quantity} kits, the recorded commitment is: {commitment}. Please use those terms when you review the plan.

questions.label: Could you accept a split delivery?

actors.name: Sam
actors.scope: Shipping budget, escalation boundaries and a clear handoff.

questions.label: What shipping budget can I use?
questions.response: This shift has {budget} shipping units. A departure is charged once when it is used, even if several orders share it. I cannot increase the budget in this exercise.

questions.label: What needs to be in my handoff?
questions.response: Leave the recorded plan, current stock assumptions, accepted customer changes and unresolved commitments visible. A handoff can be complete while a delivery problem is still open; make that distinction clear.

questions.label: What if I cannot meet a customer promise?
questions.response: Keep the original promise unless the customer accepts a supported change. Record any remaining problem for the next shift. I cannot accept different terms on a customer's behalf or treat expected stock as received.
